skill.name: nextjs-devtools
skill.description: Next.js development tooling that connects to a Model Context Protocol server to inspect routes, components, build information, and configuration.
skill.summary: Inspect Next.js routes, components, build data, and configuration through an MCP client.
skill.author: 92Bilal26

security_audit.summary: The main risks are intentional command execution and unpinned npm package execution. The Python client can run a user-supplied stdio command through a shell, and the shell script and docs run npx next-devtools-mcp@latest. Network use is mostly expected MCP communication, and many static hits were Markdown formatting or session bookkeeping false positives.

remediation.suggestion: Replace shell=True with an argument list, or allow only a reviewed command template for the Next.js MCP server.
Pin next-devtools-mcp to a reviewed version and document how maintainers verify updates before changing the pin.
Require user confirmation before running bash, Python stdio, or npx commands from the skill documentation.
Warn users before connecting to non-localhost MCP URLs or sending custom HTTP headers.

content.user_title: Inspect Next.js Apps with MCP DevTools
content.value_statement: Debugging Next.js routes, components, and build settings can require many manual checks. This skill connects Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to a Next.js MCP server for focused inspection.
actual_capabilities: Starts or connects to a Next.js DevTools MCP server.
Lists available MCP tools from HTTP or stdio transports.
Calls MCP tools for routes, route details, components, build information, and configuration.
Emits MCP tool schemas as Markdown or JSON documentation.
Supports custom HTTP headers for MCP requests.
limitations: Designed for Next.js projects, not general React applications.
Requires Python 3, Node.js, npx, and access to the MCP server package.
Can execute local commands when stdio or shell scripts are used.
Does not replace manual validation of build output or security settings.

use_cases.title: Route Inventory During Refactors
use_cases.description: Inspect all application routes before changing navigation, layouts, or API paths.

use_cases.title: Build Configuration Review
use_cases.description: Check build information and Next.js configuration while diagnosing compile or deployment issues.

use_cases.title: AI-Assisted Project Inspection
use_cases.description: Let an AI coding assistant query MCP tools and summarize project structure during development.
use_cases.target_user: Claude, Codex, or Claude Code user

prompt_templates.title: List Project Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this Next.js project with the nextjs-devtools skill. List the available routes and summarize any dynamic routes.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect One Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nextjs-devtools to review the route I am working on. Explain its route details and any configuration signals that matter.

prompt_templates.title: Review Build Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nextjs-devtools to inspect build information and Next.js configuration. Identify settings that could affect deployment behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Map Route, Component, and Build Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nextjs-devtools to combine route data, component inventory, build information, and configuration. Produce a concise diagnosis for the feature area I am changing.

output_examples.input: Inspect routes before a navigation refactor.
output: A grouped route inventory for pages, app routes, and API endpoints.
A short note about dynamic routes that need extra review.

output_examples.input: Review why the build behaves differently in production.
output_examples.output: A plain-language summary of relevant build and configuration settings, with likely causes to check first.

output_examples.input: Find components related to a dashboard feature.
output_examples.output: A component inventory summary that highlights likely dashboard files and follow-up inspection targets.

best_practices: Run the skill from the root of a trusted Next.js repository.
Pin and review the MCP server package before regular use.
Prefer localhost MCP endpoints unless a remote server is explicitly trusted.
anti_patterns: Running shell commands from untrusted prompts without user review.
Sending secrets through MCP HTTP headers or tool parameters.
Using this skill for non-Next.js projects and trusting incomplete results.

faq.question: What projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It is intended for Next.js applications that can be inspected through a Next.js DevTools MCP server.

faq.question: Does it modify my application?
faq.answer: The documented tools are inspection focused, but the helper scripts can start local processes.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: It can connect to HTTP MCP endpoints and can use npx to fetch the MCP server package.

faq.question: What should I check before installing it?
faq.answer: Review the command execution behavior, pin the npm package version, and use trusted local projects.

faq.question: Is it useful outside Next.js?
faq.answer: No. The skill is built around Next.js routes, configuration, components, and build information.
